1.title: Faith and Wisdom
1.themes: Trials, Wisdom, Faith, Hearing and Doing
1.outline:
I. Greetings (1:1)
II. Faith and Wisdom in Trials (1:2-18)
III. Hearing and Doing the Word (1:19-27)
1.summary: James encourages believers to rejoice in trials, ask God for wisdom, and ensure that their faith is active through doing the word, not just hearing it.

2.title: Faith Without Works is Dead
2.outline:
I. Warning Against Partiality (2:1-13)
II. Faith Without Works is Dead (2:14-26)
2.summary: James warns against showing favoritism to the rich and argues that genuine faith is necessarily accompanied by righteous works, illustrating this with Abraham and Rahab.

3.title: Taming the Tongue
3.outline:
I. Taming the Tongue (3:1-12)
II. Two Kinds of Wisdom (3:13-18)
3.summary: James highlights the disproportionate power of the tongue to cause harm and contrasts earthly, demonic wisdom with peace-loving, heavenly wisdom.

4.title: Submission to God
4.outline:
I. Warning Against Worldliness (4:1-12)
II. Warning Against Boasting (4:13-17)
4.summary: James addresses conflicts caused by worldly desires, calling for humility and submission to God. He also warns against arrogant boasting about tomorrow.

5.title: Patience and Prayer
5.outline:
I. Warning to the Rich (5:1-6)
II. Patience in Suffering (5:7-12)
III. The Prayer of Faith (5:13-20)
5.summary: James pronounces judgment on oppressive rich people, encourages patience among suffering believers until the Lord's return, and emphasizes the power of faithful prayer and confession.

1.title: A Living Hope
1.outline:
I. Greetings (1:1-2)
II. A Living Hope (1:3-12)
III. A Call to Holy Living (1:13-25)
1.summary: Peter praises God for the living hope and future inheritance of believers. He urges them to live holy lives in reverent fear, having been redeemed by Christ's blood.

2.title: Living Stones and Submission
2.outline:
I. The Living Stone and a Chosen People (2:1-10)
II. Living Honorably (2:11-12)
III. Submission to Authority (2:13-25)
2.summary: Peter describes believers as living stones built into a spiritual house. He instructs them to submit to human authorities and endure unjust suffering, following Christ's example.

3.title: Wives, Husbands, and Righteous Suffering
3.themes: Marriage, Righteousness, Suffering for Doing Good
3.outline:
I. Wives and Husbands (3:1-7)
II. Suffering for Righteousness (3:8-22)
3.summary: Peter provides instructions for godly marriages. He encourages believers to pursue peace and to be prepared to suffer for doing good, just as Christ suffered for sins.

4.title: Living for God
4.outline:
I. Living for God (4:1-11)
II. Suffering for Being a Christian (4:12-19)
4.summary: Peter urges believers to live for God's will rather than human desires, to use their spiritual gifts to serve others, and to rejoice when participating in the sufferings of Christ.

5.title: Shepherding the Flock
5.outline:
I. To the Elders and the Flock (5:1-11)
II. Final Greetings (5:12-14)
5.summary: Peter instructs elders to shepherd God's flock willingly and humbly. He advises all believers to be humble, cast their anxieties on God, and remain vigilant against the devil.

1.title: Making Calling and Election Sure
1.outline:
I. Greetings (1:1-2)
II. Making Calling and Election Sure (1:3-15)
III. The Prophetic Word Confirmed (1:16-21)
1.summary: Peter exhorts believers to supplement their faith with virtue and knowledge to make their calling sure. He affirms the reliability of the prophetic word and his eyewitness testimony of Christ's majesty.

2.title: False Prophets and Teachers
2.outline:
I. The Danger of False Teachers (2:1-3)
II. God's Judgment on the Wicked (2:4-10a)
III. Description of False Teachers (2:10b-22)
2.summary: Peter warns of false teachers who will secretly introduce destructive heresies. He uses historical examples to show that God will judge the unrighteous and rescue the godly.

3.title: The Day of the Lord
3.outline:
I. The Certainty of Christ's Coming (3:1-13)
II. Final Exhortations (3:14-18)
3.summary: Peter addresses scoffers who doubt the Second Coming, explaining that God's delay is due to His patience, desiring all to repent. He urges believers to live holy lives in anticipation of the new heavens and new earth.

1.title: Walking in the Light
1.outline:
I. The Word of Life (1:1-4)
II. Walking in the Light (1:5-10)
1.summary: John proclaims the reality of the incarnate Christ and declares that God is light. He explains that fellowship with God requires walking in the light and confessing sins to receive forgiveness.

2.title: Love and Antichrists
2.themes: Obedience, Love for the World, Antichrists
2.outline:
I. Christ Our Advocate (2:1-6)
II. The New Commandment (2:7-14)
III. Do Not Love the World (2:15-17)
IV. Warning Against Antichrists (2:18-29)
2.summary: John presents Christ as our advocate and emphasizes that knowing God involves keeping His commandments. He warns against loving the world and cautions believers about antichrists who deny Jesus.

3.title: Children of God
3.outline:
I. Children of God (3:1-10)
II. Love One Another (3:11-24)
3.summary: John marvels at the love that calls believers children of God. He contrasts children of God with children of the devil, stating that those born of God practice righteousness and genuinely love their brothers and sisters.

4.title: Testing the Spirits and God's Love
4.themes: Truth, God is Love, Fearless Love
4.outline:
I. Testing the Spirits (4:1-6)
II. God is Love (4:7-21)
4.summary: John instructs believers to test spirits to see if they acknowledge Jesus came in the flesh. He profoundly states that God is love, and since God loved us, we also ought to love one another, which casts out fear.

5.title: Faith and Eternal Life
5.outline:
I. Overcoming the World (5:1-5)
II. Testimony Concerning the Son (5:6-12)
III. That You May Know (5:13-21)
5.summary: John emphasizes that faith in Jesus as the Son of God is the victory that overcomes the world. He writes so that believers may know they have eternal life and have confidence in prayer.

1.title: Walking in Truth and Love
1.outline:
I. Greeting (1-3)
II. Walking in Truth and Love (4-6)
III. Warning Against Deceivers (7-11)
IV. Final Greetings (12-13)
1.summary: John writes to the 'elect lady and her children,' rejoicing that they are walking in truth. He exhorts them to love one another and warns them not to show hospitality to false teachers who deny the incarnation.

1.title: Hospitality and Opposition
1.outline:
I. Greeting to Gaius (1-4)
II. Praise for Gaius's Hospitality (5-8)
III. Diotrephes's Opposition (9-10)
IV. Demetrius's Good Testimony and Conclusion (11-15)
1.summary: John commends Gaius for his faithful hospitality to traveling missionaries. He contrasts this with the prideful and obstructive behavior of Diotrephes, while affirming the good testimony of Demetrius.

1.title: Contending for the Faith
1.outline:
I. Greeting (1-2)
II. The Call to Contend for the Faith (3-4)
III. God's Judgment on the Ungodly (5-16)
IV. Call to Persevere (17-23)
V. Doxology (24-25)
1.summary: Jude urgently appeals to believers to contend for the faith against ungodly intruders who pervert God's grace. He reminds them of past judgments and urges them to persevere in God's love, ending with a magnificent doxology.
